This reference image is an excellent match — same white cottony mycelium, identical dark irregular sclerotia, same tan/brown background tissue, and even the same Bugwood image series (1572830 vs 1572833). Now checking 3 more classes as required.

**Summary of analysis:**

- **Test image key features**: White cottony mycelium on stems/plant tissue, dark irregular clustered sclerotia embedded in the mycelium, tan/brown necrotic tissue underneath
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot reference (Bugwood_14 = #1572833)**: Identical features — same white fluffy mycelium, same dark irregular sclerotia on stems, same Bugwood image series as the test image (#1572830), same photographer/dataset
- **Southern_Blight**: Shows field-level wilting, no close-up mycelium/sclerotia match
- **Gray_Mold**: Microscopic conidiophores, not matching
- **Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers**: Microscopic conidia, not matching

The white cottony mycelium with dark, irregular, multi-lobed sclerotia is the hallmark of *Sclerotinia sclerotiorum* (Timber Rot). Southern Blight (*Sclerotium rolfsii*) produces small round mustard-seed-like tan sclerotia, not the dark irregular ones seen here.
